subject: DPA & Integration SLA — QBit redlines and procurement timeline
messages:
From: Emma Porter <emma.porter@qbit.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: QBit Legal <legal@qbit.com>, QBit Procurement <procurement@qbit.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBit DPA redlines and integration SLAs

Hi Sergio / Marissa —

Thanks again for last week's demo. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the templated DPA and surfaced a handful of clauses we need clarified before procurement can issue an LOI. I've attached QBit's annotated DPA (QBit_DPA_redlines_v2.docx). Top items so you can triage: 

- Data retention: we need a 5-year retention maximum for logs containing customer PII; requests for deletion should be processed in 30 days.
- Subprocessors: require prior written notice + 10 business day objection window.
- Security: want explicit mention of encryption at rest for backups and KMS key control.
- Incident SLA: 72-hour notification + 2-week remediation plan is too long for us — prefer 48-hour notification and 7-day mitigation milestones.
- SLA & credits: requested 99.9% availability target and a simplified credit table.

For the integration SOW, procurement wants the milestone-based acceptance criteria and a defined support window for go-live. I've included an integration_scope_SOW_v1.pdf with comments. Can you confirm Redwood's stance on the above and provide an updated DPA redline by Tuesday?

Best,
Emma Porter
Contracts Lead, QBit Analytics

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Porter <emma.porter@qbit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBit DPA redlines and integration SLAs

Emma —

Appreciate the clear summary and the annotated copy. Marissa will lead commercial/procurement, and I've looped in Laura from legal to run the redlines. High-level responses:

- Retention / deletion: we can support a 5-year retention cap for logs containing customer PII; standard operational logs that are non-PII are scoped separately. We'll commit to 30-day deletion processing for verified requests.
- Subprocessors: prior notice with a 10-business-day objection window is acceptable; we ask that objections be limited to material security/compliance concerns.
- Encryption / KMS: Redwood uses customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we use our managed KMS with keys segregated per-tenant. We'll add explicit 'encryption at rest' language and clarify key control options in the DPA.
- Incident notification: we can move to 48-hour initial notification. For remediation milestones we'll propose a 7/14/30 day track depending on severity — Laura will propose precise language.
- SLA: 99.9% for the integration path is plausible; need to sync on measurement windows and credit calculation.

We'll aim to return a redline (rdw_response_DPA_redline.docx) by EOD Tue. Marissa — can you own procurement timeline and confirm whether QBit needs a signed LOI before final DPA?

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Porter <emma.porter@qbit.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBit DPA redlines and integration SLAs

Emma / team —

Thanks for the redlines — we reviewed with infra and product (cc Karthik). A few clarifications and proposed edits to keep commercial momentum while protecting both parties: 

1) Retention / deletion
- We will accept a 5-year cap on retention for records that contain customer PII, but we need to carve out ephemeral telemetry that is aggregated and non-identifiable. We'll add a definition and an example list in Section 2.
- Deletion: 30 calendar days for standard deletion requests; for requests requiring downstream data reconciliation (e.g., replicated backups) we'll commit to completion as soon as reasonably practicable and notify QBit of expected timelines.

2) Subprocessors
- Prior written notice + 10 business days objection window OK. We'll include a process for emergency onboarding of subprocessors with retroactive notice for critical security patches.

3) KMS & encryption
- For hosted customers: we commit to AES-256 encryption at rest and will offer a customer-key option via BYOK on Dedicated and Private tiers. We'll add the exact KMS options to Schedule 1.

4) Incident response and SLA
- 48-hour initial notification is acceptable. Proposed remediation milestones: initial containment plan within 7 days for high severity; full remediation timeline will be mutually agreed per incident severity.
- SLA measurement: monthly uptime measured by model endpoint availability; propose 99.9% with a 30-day measurement window and a prorated credit table (we'll include sample calculations in the redline).

5) Data export / portability
- We'll provide machine-readable data exports upon termination; format and scope will be specified in the SOW.

I'll attach a marked-up response (rdw_response_DPA_redline.docx) with exact language. Karthik: please review the SOW attachment and confirm the go-live support window (we suggested 2 weeks of 24/5 on-call + 90-day standard support).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Emma Porter <emma.porter@qbit.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBit DPA redlines and integration SLAs

Marissa / Emma —

Quick note on the SOW and acceptance criteria:
- We'll define two milestone gates: sandbox integration (sign-off by QBit engineering on API / feature parity) and staged production rollout (defined uplift tests and sampling).
- Go-live support: 2 weeks of 24/5 on-call coverage from Redwood engineers, followed by 90 days of priority support (business hours). Any paid extended support can be quoted separately.
- Responsibilities: Redwood to provide API specs, SDK, and a runbook for incident triage; QBit to provide test data and a point-of-contact for validation.

If that aligns, Marissa can fold into procurement timeline and we can attach the SOW.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Porter <emma.porter@qbit.com>, QBit Procurement <procurement@qbit.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBit DPA redlines and integration SLAs

Emma —

Thanks — appreciate the speed on this. Procurement item: an LOI would accelerate legal review on your side, but not strictly required prior to signature. If your procurement team prefers to lock terms earlier, we can provide a short-form LOI outlining agreed commercial points (term, committed seats/usage, target go-live date 2027-01-15) and a mutual confidentiality line. Please advise which you prefer; if LOI, we can send a draft by EOD today.

Attached: integration_scope_SOW_v1.pdf (with Karthik's acceptance gates noted). Laura will post the official DPA redline to the DocuSign link once the team agrees to the technical edits.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Porter <emma.porter@qbit.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: QBit Legal <legal@qbit.com>, QBit Procurement <procurement@qbit.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBit DPA redlines and integration SLAs

Marissa / team —

This is great — LOI would be helpful to lock commercial terms while legal finishes the DPA. Please send the LOI draft and we'll get procurement to sign off. We're aligned on the technical items; procurement asked that the SLA credit table be simplified a bit (examples are helpful). Appreciate the quick turnaround — if Laura can push the redline to DocuSign we can route internally and aim to sign by next Wed.

Emily (procurement) will be watching the DocuSign link. Thanks all — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Emma
Contracts Lead, QBit Analytics
